avoid_supplements.name: Anticholinergic herbs (Jimsonweed, Datura, Henbane)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive anticholinergic effects leading to urinary retention, constipation, tachycardia, and cognitive impairment
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; counsel patient to avoid completely

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce tiotropium bioavailability and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discuss alternative supplements with healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Grapeseed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly increase tiotropium levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic effects; no dose adjustment typically needed

caution_supplements.name: Ginger (high doses)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild anticholinergic properties; additive effects possible at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Limit ginger supplementation to moderate culinary amounts

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly delay absorption of tiotropium; clinical significance minimal for maintenance therapy
caution_foods.action: Take tiotropium consistently with or without food; maintain consistent routine

monitoring_notes: Tiotropium has minimal hepatic metabolism and low systemic bioavailability; primary monitoring should focus on anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, tachycardia) especially in elderly patients or those with BPH/narrow-angle glaucoma. Counsel patients on proper inhalation technique and consistent daily use for optimal respiratory outcomes.
